$comment: Third-party container images the family mirrors into its own registry.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (G44). OpenMetadata ships from docker.getcollate.io, a
vendor registry backed by neither Docker Hub nor GHCR. Four repositories pull
it, every one of them on a nightly cron, so an outage there fails unattended
and reads as a broken governance step rather than as somebody else's
registry. Measured on 2026-08-22: two of seven acceptance runs died at
`make up` with a TLS handshake timeout, and the rerun died again with
`connection reset by peer`, so the bounded retry fabric-emulator already
carries would not have saved either.
WHAT MAY GO IN HERE. An image the family DEPENDS ON at runtime and does not
build, whose registry is not one the family already trusts. Docker Hub and
GHCR are trusted, so opensearchproject/opensearch is deliberately absent: it
is on Hub, and mirroring it would add a copy to keep in step for no
availability gain.
upstream     the vendor reference, tag included
mirror       the GHCR repository it is copied to
index        the digest of the MIRROR's manifest index, recorded by
`scripts/mirror_images.py --push` and enforced by --check
upstream_index  the digest the copy was made FROM, so a tag that moves
under us is visible rather than silently adopted
platforms    the (os/arch) pairs the index must carry. Both images are
multi-arch, and a mirror made with pull/tag/push instead of
`buildx imagetools create` collapses the index to the
runner's architecture -- which keeps CI green on amd64 while
breaking every arm64 laptop. Recorded so the check can fail
for it.
